basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; persistent strabismus affects 3/8 patients (~38%). Hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
Benign ovarian epithelial neoplasm; reproductive organs have no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Hereditary displacement of the carpal bones affects the wrist skeleton and joints.
Inherited axonal degeneration directly affects peripheral nerves and sometimes the CNS; weakness and gait impairment are neurologic consequences.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 19/19 patients.
Benign neoplasm confined to breast ductal lobular units; breast has no axis.
Benign reactive lymphoid proliferation resembling lymphoma; immune-mediated lymphoid hyperplasia supports these axes. No specific extranodal organ is established.
Defined by toxic cardiac conduction dysfunction and toxic encephalopathy. Nausea and visual disturbances alone do not establish gastrointestinal or ocular injury.
Leptospiral infection; thrombocytopenia occurs in 30-79%. Hepatitis, kidney injury and meningitis occur in <30%; frequent enzyme elevations alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome defined by optic atrophy, peripheral neuropathy, ataxia and developmental impairment; optic atrophy occurs in 80-99%.
Tumor located in the eyelid, which belongs to the ocular axis; no additional organ involvement is established.
Inherited disorder of generalized cutaneous pigmentation; no common extracutaneous damage is established.
Congenital neuronal migration abnormality producing heterotopic bands within the brain.
Neonatal insulin deficiency and hyperglycemia define the disease. Frequent macroglossia lacks documented functional damage; other organ abnormalities occur in <30%.
Acquired DIC and vascular thrombosis, usually infectious or immune-mediated; cutaneous necrosis is defining, with blistering and gangrene in 30-79%. Other organ failure is <30%.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Obesity and limb abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); dysmorphism alone does not establish organ damage.
Malignant stromal neoplasm originating in breast; breast has no axis. Sarcomatous differentiation does not establish disease in muscle or bone.
Benign neoplasm arising in the renal cortex.
Primary podocyte injury and glomerular scarring define the disease; proposed circulating permeability factors alone do not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Congenital cystic spinal cord malformation associated with a spina bifida vertebral defect. Common additional organ damage is not established across subtypes.
Sideroblastic anemia is a disorder of erythropoiesis and heme synthesis. Common independent hepatic injury is not established for this subtype.
Citrin-related metabolic disease defined by hyperammonemic encephalopathy; hepatic fibrosis in 11/14 (~79%) and steatosis in 17/19 (~89%). Pancreatitis in 5/19 (~26%) is excluded.
Dystonic movement disorder arising from abnormal nervous system motor control; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
Inherited interstitial lung disease with parenchymal abnormalities, impaired diffusion and restrictive physiology; no separate immune mechanism is established.
Inborn metabolic disorder defined by microcephaly and psychomotor developmental impairment. Hypotonia alone does not establish direct skeletal muscle damage.
